statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6 (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, against Stress 54 (elevated) on Washington's explicit rejection of Iran's seven-day Strait of Hormuz roadmap, a ten-year Treasury yield at a two-decade high of 5.18% and roughly 70% market-implied odds of an October Fed hike into a PCE and payrolls week.
recommendation: Tail holds a 6-10 band and stays at least fifteen points below the 25 blocking threshold in every assessed hour, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON across the whole window. No danger window is published: a market that does not trade cannot supply the observed price-path evidence a narrow evidence-based window requires, and the CME reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday falls one hour beyond the end of this forecast. Elevated Stress describes a difficult environment that may still mean-revert and is reported separately from the Tail-derived state. Existing-position management and protection are unaffected by the Tail mapping.
headline: CME weekend halt holds Tail at 6 while Washington's rejection of Iran's Hormuz roadmap keeps Stress elevated at 54
body: Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, one hour after this forecast window closes, so every assessed hour is structurally incapable of containing an observed price path. Friday's completed session argues against pathological structure rather than for it: NDX closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.53% below its 30,770.63 52-week high, while VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 and the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closed at 51,828.62, 7,743.41 and 27,068.72 for weekly gains. That is a two-way auction closing away from both extremes, so Tail is held at 6 and the mapped state is EA_ON. Stress is a separate question and firms a point to 54. Washington has now explicitly rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap, delivered through Qatar, which would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the naval blockade of Iranian ports, waiving oil sanctions and releasing roughly $12bn in frozen assets; the strait remains closed past day 209 with commercial transits near zero, and Iranian security forces have said targets remain to be struck. That matters asymmetrically into the reopen, because part of Friday's oil easing - Brent settling 2.77% lower at 97.44 and WTI near $92 - rested on reopening optimism that Saturday removed. The rate backdrop is unchanged and heavy: the 25 September H.15 shows the two-year at 4.87%, the ten-year at 5.18% and the thirty-year at 5.47%, a two-decade high at the long end, with roughly 70% market-implied odds on an October Fed hike and final September Michigan sentiment at 48.1 against 4.6% one-year inflation expectations. PCE on 30 September and September payrolls on 2 October follow immediately. Tail therefore drifts from 6 to 10 across the window as unpriced weekend headlines accumulate into one reopening auction, which is discrete-event gap risk rather than the repeated extension after failed retracements that the elevated Tail band requires. The shared Finviz context file collected at 20:11Z reported collectionStatus partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable; its breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings are explicitly latest-session, non-real-time context and were used only as weak confirmation of Friday's orderly, chip-led tone, never as live NQ price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, so none is unavailable. The window opens at 21:00Z on Friday, immediately after the CME settlement, with Tail 12, Stress 50 and normal mode as the session's directional question closed out. Through Friday night Tail decayed from 12 to 9 and Stress eased from 50 to 47. Across Saturday the halt held Tail in an 8 then 7 then 6 band while Stress rebuilt from a 44 trough to 54 as the Hormuz diplomacy hardened and the rate backdrop stayed heavy, and Confidence drifted from 88 to 78 as the last tradable tape aged. Every hour in the window was mapped EA_ON and green, and no historical opinion has been restated using later information.
outlookSummary: All twenty-four forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00Z on Sunday, one hour past the end of this window, so no hour can contain observed price-path structure. Tail is held in a 6-10 band throughout and stays at least fifteen points below the 25 blocking threshold, mapping EA_ON and green in every slot. The drift from 6 to 7 early on Sunday and to 8, 9 and then 10 through the afternoon is accumulated unpriced gap risk ahead of a single reopening auction, not observed one-way structure, and the weekend withdrawal of Hormuz reopening optimism is the main reason that stock of unpriced news is larger than a quiet weekend would leave. Stress traces the weekend headline windows, easing to a 50 floor in the thin overnight hours, firming as the Gulf working week and then the US Sunday programme window open, and capping at 57 late on Sunday on the unresolved strait closure and a rate path that prices an October hike into a PCE and payrolls week. Confidence decays from 77 to 70 purely because the newest observable tape ages past sixty hours with no replacement possible before the reopen; the evidence base is otherwise complete on levels, yields, oil, volatility and the verified calendar.
